patch.value: Disambiguate parent object-fetch endpoints from nested objects repositories

The catalogue-first disposition for PR #91 makes tenant/objects reachable but intentionally gives the deeper repository precedence at the ambiguous path tenant/objects/fetch. Consequently a parent-scoped token cannot use that path for the tenant repository object-fetch endpoint while the nested repository exists. This is a residual wire-layout ambiguity, beyond the promised minimal catalogue-precedence fix; ordinary parent fetch and nested clone remain reachable.

An explicit wire address or compatible negotiation makes parent fetchObjects and nested repository fetch reachable together; regression tests cover no-auth, parent-only, nested-only and multi-repository grants; unauthorized requests retain the fixed denial shape.

Serve repositories tenant and tenant/objects with distinct read grants. The catalogue-precedence regression in test/serve.test.ts asserts that the nested grant fetches successfully at tenant/objects/fetch and the parent grant receives the fixed denial there. HttpTransport.fetchObjects for the parent uses the same path.
Both repositories and every supported endpoint can be addressed unambiguously, including with a grant that reaches both repositories and without authentication.
The nested repository shadows the parent objects/fetch endpoint at their shared URL path.
